questions.explanation: The henley has a short buttoned placket at the throat but no collar. The polo has a folded collar.

questions.promptText: Which one is the henley, not a plain crew tee?
questions.explanation: The buttoned placket is the henley’s tell; the crew tee has a plain round neckline.

questions.promptText: Which is the spread collar (points set wide apart)?
questions.explanation: The spread collar opens its points toward the shoulders, leaving a wide throat gap. The point collar sits closer together.
A button-down pins its points to the shirt with two small buttons, keeping a soft roll. The point collar has no such buttons.

questions.promptText: Which is the oxford-cloth shirt (a basket-weave with body), not chambray?
questions.explanation: Oxford cloth pairs two fine threads against a thicker one in a basket-weave, giving body. Chambray is a smoother plain weave that reads like light denim.

questions.promptText: Which is the Chelsea boot (elastic side panels, no laces)?
questions.explanation: The Chelsea pulls on via elastic gore panels and has no laces. The chukka/desert boot has two or three lace eyelets.

questions.promptText: Which is the flat-front chino, not the five-pocket jean?
questions.explanation: The chino runs a smooth cotton twill with no rivets and no coin pocket. The jean shows the five-pocket layout and rivets at the stress points.

questions.promptText: Which is the derby (a lace-up with open lacing)?
questions.explanation: The derby laces up, with the lace flaps stitched on top of the shoe front. The loafer has no laces at all: you just step in.
